title: Matching resumes to roles with embeddings
summary: Find the most relevant candidates for a role among millions of resumes, and show why.
context: Ragi Careers holds 4 million resumes. Recruiters write a role in plain words and want a ranked list within two seconds, with the reasons. Keyword search misses a 'backend engineer' who wrote 'server-side developer', and it is easy to stuff with terms.
Resumes are updated daily, and a person who deleted their profile must vanish from results at once. Costs have to stay small: embeddings are computed by a model billed per use.
must_handle: A search returns in about two seconds.
Hard rules hold, such as location and years of experience.
Each result gives a reason a recruiter can check.
A deleted profile stops appearing immediately.
A change of embedding model does not need downtime.
show_in_answer: How resumes become searchable, and when they are re-embedded.
How one search runs, from text to a ranked list.
How filters and similarity work together.
How you would judge quality without many labelled examples.
